title: Curated internal indirect-call subset: real configured libcurl
analyzer_blind_declaration: Selected, read, justified and frozen without seeing either Yasa C or CodeGraph C predictions for this project.

scope.population: 11 manually selected syntactic indirect-call sites in libcurl, across five callback mechanisms.
scope.selection_basis: Readable bounded internal target provenance, mechanism diversity and high confidence; no tool predictions were used to select sites.
scope.closed_world_boundary: Supported libcurl API executions and libcurl-internal callers of private Curl_* routines; valid objects and no memory corruption. External caller-supplied callbacks are excluded from target enumeration.
scope.target_meaning: The complete set of project-internal functions that can be called at this selected source expression over valid executions under this configuration.
scope.identity: Repository-relative file::function; disambiguates static functions and aligns with file-aware build gold.
not_claimed: A complete inventory of indirect calls
Proof of all runtime path feasibility beyond the documented registration and normal protocol use
scope.metric_guidance: Report recall only as curated-indirect-subset recall (11 sites / 25 site-target edges). If an analyzer emits only caller-to-callee edges, report that representation explicitly; these selected pairs are unique even after erasing site locations. Do not label missing target pairs false positives or extrapolate this subset to all callbacks.

sites.execution_guard: The protocol has run its PINGPONG_SETUP and rc indicates socket readiness or buffered input.
sites.rationale: There are exactly four PINGPONG_SETUP invocations in lib/, and no other member assignments; all four protocols are enabled.
sites.limitations: This is a union across real FTP, IMAP, POP3 and SMTP connection objects at the generic pingpong site. A particular connection has exactly its own protocol pair. Other protocol handlers are not pingpong registrations and are not targets.

sites.execution_guard: The wildcard object and its destructor member are non-null.
sites.rationale: The internal wildcard state begins zeroed; FTP wildcard initialization supplies the sole non-null destructor assignment, and cleanup/failure only clear it.

mime_table.rationale: The only encoder object table: five named encodings, four distinct read implementations and three distinct size implementations; the last entry is a null sentinel.

mime_assignment.rationale: curl_mime_encoder assigns either null or an address from encoders; the public API accepts a name, not a function pointer.

mime_copy.rationale: Duplication copies an existing encoder pointer; it introduces no new encoder implementation.

mime_guard_read.rationale: The encoded-read routine is entered only for non-null part->encoder.

md5_params.rationale: The only MD5_params initializer binds init/update/final to my_md5_*.

md5_store.rationale: The MD5 context retains exactly the supplied parameter object.

md5_call_digest.rationale: Digest auth supplies Curl_DIGEST_MD5; the other three initializations in this file do the same.

hmac_md5.rationale: MD5 HMAC parameter object binds the three my_md5_* implementations.

hmac_sha256.rationale: SHA256 HMAC parameter object binds the three my_sha256_* implementations.

hmac_cram.rationale: CRAM-MD5 creates a context with Curl_HMAC_MD5.

hmac_forward.rationale: Curl_hmacit forwards the same parameter object to Curl_HMAC_init.

hmac_store.rationale: The context retains the supplied hash parameter object.

hmac_final_alias.rationale: The finalization local alias comes from the retained context hash.

unused_sha512_params.rationale: A SHA512/256 HMAC object exists, but no lib/ caller passes or otherwise references it. Its presence alone does not make it a possible target at the selected HMAC sites.

pp_macro.snippet:
#define PINGPONG_SETUP(pp, s, e) \
  do {                           \
    (pp)->statemachine = s;      \
    (pp)->endofresp = e;         \
  } while(0)
pp_macro.rationale: PINGPONG_SETUP writes the protocol-specific pair of implementations.

pp_ftp.rationale: FTP connection setup installs only FTP implementations.

pp_imap.rationale: IMAP connection setup installs only IMAP implementations.

pp_pop3.rationale: POP3 connection setup installs only POP3 implementations.

pp_smtp.rationale: SMTP connection setup installs only SMTP implementations.

wc_alloc.rationale: Wildcard state is internal and zero allocated.

wc_assignment.snippet:
wildcard->ftpwc = ftpwc; /* put it to the WildcardData tmp pointer */
  wildcard->dtor = wc_data_dtor;
wc_assignment.rationale: The sole non-null assignment to WildcardData.dtor is the FTP wildcard cleanup function.

wc_clear.rationale: Failure clears the callback; it does not install another target.

external_mime_assignment.rationale: The public curl_mime_data_cb API accepts arbitrary application read/seek/free callbacks. These three dispatch families cannot have complete closed project-internal target sets.

excluded_external_callback_inventory.reason: A public API can install arbitrary application callbacks. Some branches can also use internal helpers; that does not bound the whole site to project-internal targets.

manual_cross_reference_checks.MD5_params: rg over lib/ found only Curl_DIGEST_MD5 as an initializer. Curl_MD5_init arguments: pop3.c:574 and vauth/digest.c:405,419,442,460, all &Curl_DIGEST_MD5.
manual_cross_reference_checks.HMAC_params: lib/ argument sources: vauth/cram.c:60 is &Curl_HMAC_MD5; http_aws_sigv4.c:43 and vtls/vtls_scache.c:809,1165,1203 are &Curl_HMAC_SHA256; hmac.c:151 forwards its argument. http_httpsig.c:511 also uses SHA256 but is disabled. Curl_HMAC_SHA512_256 has only a declaration and definition in lib/, no use as an argument.
manual_cross_reference_checks.mime_encoder: Only non-null origin is encoders in curl_mime_encoder; mime.c:1214 copies an existing encoder. The object is internal; there is no callback registration API for its encodefunc or sizefunc.
manual_cross_reference_checks.pingpong: Only macro PINGPONG_SETUP assigns statemachine/endofresp; exactly four invocations exist in lib/: ftp.c:3540, imap.c:2289, pop3.c:1436, smtp.c:1685.
manual_cross_reference_checks.wildcard: WildcardData.dtor starts zeroed; ftp.c:4004 assigns wc_data_dtor, ftp.c:4031 and ftplistparser.c:198 clear it; no other non-null assignment found. Generic unrelated structs also named dtor were not merged.
